answer: Increasing marginal registration cost uses a river of sequential fee tiers: each new identity an operator registers costs more than the last, so a flood of fakes hits a rising wall. The enforcement rule prices each slot at base times two to the power of prior registrations from that funding source. A reef of cheap early identities gives way to prohibitive late ones, forcing attackers to pay exponentially more per fake. Costs compound like a dune building grain by grain, so mass duplication collapses under its own price curve.
